content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper demonstrates the advantage of combining Feature Optimization (FO) with Quantum Kitchen Sink (QKS) and Tree Tensor Network (TTN) in image classification process. The paper compared the baseline performance of QKS, QKS+TTN and QKS+TTN+FO to illustrate that QKS+TTN+FO can provide a significantly boost to the overall performance.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
About Challenge: Medium 
- The task of MNIST handwritten number classification itself is not challenging. The main challenge of this paper is the theory development and application of QKS+TTN+FO. 

About Contribution:  Fundamental
- The main contribution of this paper is to give a sufficient theoretical development of QKS+TTN+FO method, in both the main section and appendix.
- Another author-claimed contribution is the efficiency and effectiveness of QKS+TTN+FO method, which can be cast doubt on.

This paper is not satisfactory due to the following aspects: 
- The testing data set (handwritten digits “3” and “5” from MNIST dataset) is over-specified and inappropriate to demonstrate the effectiveness of the method. 
- The paper merely compares QKS+TTN+FO with the baseline performance of QKS and QKS+TTN, which failed to compare to other existing high-performance solutions; thus lowing the significance of the conclusion.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
About Novelty: Low
- Image classification problem itself is an intensively developed domain; however, the trail of solving the problem using QKS+TTN+FO is unique. The paper’s novelty is diminished due to the narrowed data set on only handwritten digits “3” and “5”, which fails to illustrate the advantage and generality, especially far from CIFAR-10, ImageNet, etc.

About Organization: Need to be polished. 
- The exposition and presentation of the paper need to be polished.
- The figures in the paper seem to be repetitive the word size of the figure caption is incorrect. 
- The paper also contains large batch of plain describing text with equations inlayed (etc. page 4, 6), which hinders the reading efficiency.
content.summary_of_the_review:
Overall comment and future advise
- The paper provides a detailed theoretical demonstration to the method of QKS+TTN+FO; however, the paper used an over-specified data set to demonstrate the advantage of QKS+TTN+FO, which is inconclusive without testing the method with a more sophisticated data set and comparing it with existing high-performance method.
- The main contribution of this paper is to provide a theoretical development QKS+TTN+FO, which can be a good start to explore the potential of QKS+TTN+FO; however, due to the limited progress and achievement, this paper shall not be accepted for ICLR 2023.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper the authors introduce an measurement based reduction of quantum circuits for the purpose of initialization of VQA algorithm for learning classification task. The main contribution is based on a multi-measurement step where encoded features are stochastically filtered and then provided to the VQA for learning. the paper is written in a readable form.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
While the paper is clear about its intention its contribution remains controversial. The main contribution comes from the stochastic filtering of the features that require to be run a large enough of ties to give a good approximation of the relevant features. The introduced feature optimization using gradient descent. While all the introduced elements works well for the presented concept case of MNIST an ablation experiment is needed to show the fact that the TTN is useful. simply connecting all the initialized featured to gradient descent would be interesting to see to double comparison of  the differences. 

The model requires further deeper insight on the impact of the individual components.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
In this paper, a modification of the variational quantum circuit known as Quantum Kitchen Sinks [Wilson et al., 2018] is proposed by replacing the Support Vector Machine (SVM) output classifier by a Tensor Network (TN) with tree structure (TTN). 
The model is trained on a binary MNIST dataset (only 3s and 5s) and the authors showed that the new model outperforms the original one when features are learned rather than chosen at random as in the original algorithm. 
The proposed algorithm requires a small number of qubits to be implemented on near-term quantum devices.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
-	The proposed algorithm provides a realistic potential implementation of machine learning classifier on a quantum device.
Weaknesses
-	The contribution of the paper is an incremental improvement from a previously proposed quantum machine learning algorithm [Wilson et al., 2018].
-	Experimental results are rather limited:
a)	The paper lacks from a comparison against classical (non-quantum) classification algorithms such as multilayer neural networks. The included experimental results only compare the proposed model against QKS-SVM [Wilson et al., 2018]. 
b)	Only binary MNIST dataset is considered
-	The paper is difficult to read for a non-expert on previously proposed quantum machine learning algorithms. The explanation of the baseline algorithm, the QKS-SVM [Wilson et al., 2018] is not enough for a general reader to understand the methods. Some terms are not clearly defined, for example, the concept of “coherent quantum processing” is not properly introduced.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity requires improvement in order to allow non-expert readers to follow the paper and better understand its results and contributions.
Experimental results quality could be greatly improved by considering other datasets and including also classical (non-quantum) classifiers.
Novelty is limited since it can be considered as an incremental contribution.
content.summary_of_the_review: I found the paper as an incremental improvement from a previously proposed quantum machine learning algorithm. The experimental analysis are rather weak and could be greatly improved. The clarity of the paper is also a weak point since it is difficult to follow for a non-expert on the previously proposed quantum machine learning algorithm.
